items.bewering: Stoomenjins het al lank voor die trein water uit myne gepomp.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Newcomen atmospheric engine (1712, used mainly to pump water from mines); National Coal Mining Museum for England, 'The Rise of the Steam Engine' (mine drainage drove the steam engine about a century before it was used for transport). Volledige nagaan in hierdie ronde; geen inligting oor wat verander het nie.

items.bewering: Daardie pompe was te swaar om op wiele te ry.
items.bron: Linda Hall Library, Scientist of the Day: Richard Trevithick (Newcomen and Watt low-pressure engines were good for pumping mines but too heavy and too slow for a locomotive; Trevithick's high-pressure engine was small enough to put on wheels).

items.bewering: Die trein se enjin is baie later gebou.
items.bron: Newcomen 1712 against Trevithick's Penydarren locomotive 1804 (Wikipedia, Newcomen atmospheric engine; Museum Wales, Trevithick's Penydarren locomotive); NCM gives about a century between mine pumping and transport.

items.bewering: Hierdie enjin begin by 'n vuur wat 'n ketel vol water warm maak. Werkers skep steenkool in die vuur, en die water kook.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Tender (rail) (the fireman spends much of his time shovelling coal or throwing wood into the firebox to keep steam pressure); Midcontinent Railway Museum (fireman shovels coal from the tender into the firebox by hand). Some engines burned wood or coke, but coal is the normal case and the sentence makes no 'always' claim.

items.bewering: Die kokende water verander in stoom wat baie meer plek opneem.
items.bron: University of Illinois Physics Van Q&A 'Water Expanding the Most' (water expands about 1600 times when it turns to steam at atmospheric pressure).

items.bewering: Die ketel is 'n toe houer en hou al daardie stoom vas. Die stoom druk daarom hard teen die wande van die ketel.
items.bron: University of Illinois Physics Van Q&A (in a closed strong box the water cannot expand, so pressure builds); Wikipedia, Firebox (steam engine) (boiler pressure acts on the firebox sheets and stays).

items.bewering: Sterk pype lei die stoom na 'n noue silinder met 'n suier daarin. Daar stoot die stoom die suier van die een kant na die ander.
items.bron: steamlocomotives.org, The Parts of a Steam Locomotive (steam delivered to the valve chests and cylinders, where it pushes the pistons); Wikipedia, Piston rod (steam engine cylinders nearly always double-acting, i.e. steam pushes the piston both ways). 'noue' describes a close-fitting cylinder; no factual issue, wording is the language step's concern.

items.bewering: Die suier beweeg heen en weer, maar 'n wiel moet ronddraai. 'n Sterk stang loop van die suier na 'n pen op die wiel.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Piston rod (piston rod to crosshead to connecting rod, which drives the driving wheels); steamlocomotives.org (linkage carries the piston's push to a crank on the driving wheel); US patent 454229 (main rod turns on the crankpin of the driver). The lesson folds piston rod, crosshead and connecting rod into one 'stang'; at Grade 4 this simplifies without misleading, since the chain does run from the piston to a pin on the wheel.

items.bewering: Elke stoot van die suier draai die wiel 'n stukkie verder.
items.bron: Bu.edu.eg lecture 'Types of Locomotives' and steamlocomotives.org (main rod converts the piston's back-and-forth motion into rotation of the driving wheels, stroke by stroke).

items.bewering: Daardie wiel is een van die enjin se eie wiele op die spore. So trek die enjin homself en die vrag agter hom, en ons noem hom 'n lokomotief.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster definition as reproduced (a self-propelled vehicle that runs on rails and is used for moving railroad cars); Vocabulary.com (self-propelled engine used to draw trains along railway tracks).

items.bewering: Sy vuur brand in 'n vuurkas binne die ketel, met water rondom en bo daardie kas.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Firebox (steam engine) (in the locomotive boiler the firebox is surrounded by water except for the bottom, which is open but covered by the grates; the crown sheet must be covered by water at all times).

items.bewering: Agter die lokomotief haak werkers 'n lang ry waens en trokke vas. Die waens dra mense, en die trokke dra vrag soos steenkool. Die enjin en die hele ry agter hom is saam 'n trein.
items.bron: weet.co.za, 'Spoorweë' (a train is a row of coupled iron-wheeled vehicles; passenger trains carry people, goods trains carry anything from cars to maize and coal). The fact (people in one kind of vehicle, freight such as coal in another, all coupled behind the engine) is confirmed. The Afrikaans word split waens/trokke is a usage question; no source contradicted it and it was not judged here.

items.bewering: 'n Wa se wiele sak weg in die sand en modder van 'n gewone pad. 'n Trein se wiele loop op twee gladde stawe. Die harde spoor dra die gewig, en die wiele sak nie weg nie.
items.bron: Nicholas Wood, A Practical Treatise on Rail-Roads (1825), reproduced at e-rara.ch (a horse conveys a far greater weight on a rail-road than on a common road, about 42 cwt against 17 cwt); technicshistory.com, 'High Pressure, Part 2' (a horse hauled several times as much on rails as on an eighteenth-century road). Mapping checked: the wagon-on-road against wheel-on-rail comparison rests on the real cause, less rolling resistance on a hard smooth surface; a learner reasoning further from it reaches nothing false.

items.bewering: Die spoor hou die trein ook op een pad.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Train wheel (the conical tread keeps the train aligned with the track and the flange keeps it on the rails at the limits). The lesson does not say how, so it claims nothing about tread or flange.

items.bewering: Daarom trek een enjin 'n vrag wat osse op 'n pad nie sou kon roer nie.
items.bron: Museum Wales, Trevithick's Penydarren locomotive (the first run in 1804 hauled ten tons of iron and many passengers); Wood 1825 via e-rara.ch (rails multiply what a draught animal can move). Note for a person, not a fault: 'daarom' credits the rails alone, although the engine's power plays a part too; the sentence remains true because the rails are what make such a load movable at all.

items.bewering: In 1804 het iemand anders se stoomenjin in Brittanje 'n vrag op spore getrek.
items.bron: Museum Wales, Trevithick's Penydarren locomotive; Wikipedia, Merthyr Tramroad (21 February 1804, Penydarren to Abercynon, Wales, ten tons of iron plus passengers). Wales is in Britain. Sources differ on iron or coal as the load; the lesson says only 'n vrag, so the disagreement does not touch it.

items.bewering: George Stephenson het jare later gehelp om die spoorlyn tussen Liverpool en Manchester te bou.
items.bron: University of Liverpool Victoria Gallery & Museum blog, 'Liverpool and Manchester Railway' (2020); Stephenson was appointed the line's engineer in 1824. 'gehelp om te bou' understates his role as engineer but is true.

items.bewering: Daardie lyn is in 1830 geopen en het mense sowel as vrag gedra.
items.bron: University of Liverpool Victoria Gallery & Museum blog (opened 15 September 1830; an inter-city passenger and freight railway).

items.bewering: Mense kon 'n kaartjie koop en op 'n vaste tyd ry.
items.bron: University of Liverpool Victoria Gallery & Museum blog (a timetabled service with steam-hauled carriages); Pen & Sword, The Liverpool and Manchester Railway: An Operating History (a timetabled public service for passengers and freight).

items.bewering: So het Stephenson gewys dat 'n stoomspoorlyn as 'n gewone diens kan werk.
items.bron: Implied primacy, checked as a superlative. University of Liverpool VGM blog and the Wikipedia-derived L&MR article (first inter-city railway with all trains timetabled and steam-hauled; the Stockton and Darlington of 1825 used steam only for coal trains). The careful form is already used: the lesson does not call him the inventor of the locomotive or the railway, and gives the 1804 locomotive to 'iemand anders'.

items.bewering: Voor die trein het diere en mense die trekwerk op die paaie gedoen.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Ox-wagon; Business Day / Financial Mail review 'When the ox wagon was king of the road' (2020) (ox wagons carried South Africa's road freight before rail).

items.bewering: Toe het 'n enjin die trein getrek en nie 'n dier of 'n mens nie. Een trein kon baie meer mense en vrag op een slag dra.
items.bron: Museum Wales, Penydarren (ten tons and many passengers on the first run); Worldhistory.org, Stephenson's Rocket (Rocket hauled about 13 tons at Rainhill, 1829).

items.bewering: Die trein het ook vinniger en verder gery as wat 'n span osse 'n wa kon trek.
items.bron: Business Day / Financial Mail book review (ox wagon top speed about two miles an hour); Wikipedia, Ox-wagon (about 20 km a day in good conditions); Science Museum Group, Stephenson's Rocket (averaged about 12 mph loaded at Rainhill, top speed 30 mph).

items.bewering: Spoorlyne het hawens met plekke diep in die binneland verbind.
items.blok: Wat spoorlyne aan 'n land gedoen het
items.bron: NWU Institutional Repository abstract (by 1882 lines from Cape Town, Port Elizabeth and East London reached Beaufort West, Graaff-Reinet, Cradock and Queenstown, built to link the ports with the interior); SA History Online, Aloes railway station, Port Elizabeth (prosperity from the railways to the interior).

items.bewering: Dorpe het by stasies gegroei waar die treine gestop het.
items.blok: Wat spoorlyne aan 'n land gedoen het
items.bron: Wikipedia, De Aar (junction placed on the farm De Aar in 1881; a store and hotel grew at the junction and the town was laid out and became a municipality afterwards). An AI-generated encyclopedia page that also turned up in the search was not used.

items.bewering: 'n Trein kan net ry waar iemand spore gelê het. 'n Wa of 'n dier moes die vrag van die stasie tot by die deur bring.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster as reproduced (a locomotive runs on rails); Business Day / Financial Mail review 'When the ox wagon was king of the road' (ox wagons kept carrying goods inland from the railheads).

items.bewering: Daardie laaste ent het nog lank dieselfde gebly.
items.bron: Same review as above (ox-wagon transport riders kept working beside and beyond the railways); The Henry Ford, 1926 photograph caption, and the Ox-wagon article place animal haulage well after railways arrived. The claim is vague ('nog lank') and makes no date claim that could be wrong.

items.bewering: stoom: Water wat so warm word dat dit in 'n gas verander.
items.bron: Dictionary.com, science entry for steam (water in its gaseous state, especially above the boiling point).

items.bewering: ketel: Die sterk houer waarin water gekook word om stoom onder druk te maak.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Firebox (steam engine) (boiler pressure on the firebox and boiler shell); Linda Hall Library, Richard Trevithick (high-pressure boiler and engine).

items.bewering: vuurkas: Die kas waarin 'n stoomenjin se vuur brand, by enjins wat so gebou is.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Firebox (steam engine) (the firebox is where fuel burns; some boilers, e.g. flue-type and water-tube boilers, have no separate firebox of this kind, so the hedge 'by enjins wat so gebou is' is correct).

items.bewering: suier: 'n Stewige skyf wat 'n silinder styf toemaak en daarin skuif.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Piston rod (the piston moves in the cylinder and is joined to the piston rod; steam acts on it); steamlocomotives.org, The Parts of a Steam Locomotive.

items.bewering: stoomenjin: 'n Masjien wat die druk van stoom in beweging verander.
items.bron: Linda Hall Library, Richard Trevithick (steam pressure pushes the piston); Bu.edu.eg 'Types of Locomotives' (piston motion converted into wheel rotation). The definition fits the high-pressure engine this lesson describes. Newcomen's atmospheric engine worked by atmospheric pressure acting against condensing steam. The lesson does not explain how the pumps worked, so the definition contradicts nothing in it.

items.bewering: lokomotief: Die enjin op wiele wat die trein op die spore trek.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster as reproduced; Vocabulary.com (self-propelled engine used to draw trains along railway tracks).

items.bewering: spoor: Die twee gladde stawe waarop 'n trein se wiele loop.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Train wheel (wheels run on, and are guided by, the two rails); DSAE, 'spoorweg' (spoor = track).

opsomming: Every claim was checked and confirmed. The lesson has no explicit superlatives; its one implied first, Stephenson showing that a steam railway could run as a regular service, is already in the careful form and gives the 1804 locomotive to someone else; the wagon-against-rail comparison holds as a mapping, and nothing needs fixing.
